newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT WANTS "MORE CONCRETE" BANK SELLOFF PLAN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT WANTS "MORE CONCRETE" BANK SELLOFF PLAN.

text.p: The Czech government on Wednesday called on the central bank to submit a "more concrete" plan to privatise shares in the four largest banks, Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said.
"The materials to be submitted to the government (by the central bank) will be made more concrete with a concrete proposal (on privatising the largest banks)," Klaus told a news conference.

He said he expected the materials to be submitted to the cabinet "in the coming days". A senior government official told Reuters soon after the news conference that the cabinet expectd to get the plan from the central bank "in two weeks time".

The Czech National Bank (CNB) last week said it had proposed to the cabinet a broad plan to privatise the major state stakes held in the country's "Big Four" largest banks including a suggestion of the merger of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB) savings bank Ceska Sporitelna .

The merger would create the largest banking institution in the Eastern Europe with combined assets of roughly 540 billion crowns. The CNB however proposed waiting on the final privatisation of the new combined Sporitelna and CSOB for three to five years until the effects of the merger are analysed.

Last week's CNB plan also called for fast selloff of the state's 31.5 percent stake in another bank, IPB a.s. , to a foreign partner, and for a delay in the privatisation of the state roughly 49 percent share in Komercni Banka a.s..

IPB said last week that its top management had a "constructive dialogue" in a meeting with senior officials of Nomura discussing the sale of IPB shares, but said further decisions were up to the government and central bank.
Klaus said on Wednesday he hoped the new CNB material "would go beyond" the suggestions already submitted by the central bank.

The prime minister had frowned on the suggestion of a Sporitelna/CSOB merger last weekend when he said it was akin to fusing Prague's two top soccer teams, something unthinkable for Czechs. But Klaus has praised the possibility of Nomura taking a stake in IPB.

The CNB said last week it had offered the plan from the point of view of of the banking sector regulator aiming to make Czech banks more prepared for foreign competition especially when the country enters the European Union.
